messages.content: I have the refreshed hotel screens open. Can you compare the four-night totals for The Higgins and the City Park option, including the rides we'd actually need? Also confirm that neither room is quietly priced for only two people.

Yes. Send me the final price details, room names, fees, deposit timing, and cancellation language shown for each. I’ll normalize both for two adults and your 14-year-old, then add the local transportation tied to your itinerary.

The Higgins shows two queen beds, three guests, $1,327.40 with taxes, plus a $62 destination fee each night. It says the card is charged one night now. Free cancellation until 6:00 p.m. Central on October 7. Breakfast isn't listed as included.

That makes The Higgins $1,575.40 for four nights after the $248 destination fees. The occupancy display explicitly covers three guests in the two-queen room. One night is charged when reserved, with the balance due at the hotel; cancellation is free through 6:00 p.m. Central on October 7.

The City Park place is $1,379.76 total with taxes and no resort fee. It is a king room with a sleeper sofa, and the screen says two adults and one child, age 14. Breakfast is included for all three. No charge until October 8, and cancellation is free through October 6 at 11:59 p.m. Central.

That quote also supports all three travelers, though the sleeping arrangement is one king plus the sleeper sofa rather than two permanent beds. Its complete lodging cost is $1,379.76, payment begins October 8, and the free-cancellation deadline is October 6 at 11:59 p.m. Central.
Use the museum, City Park, and music-night schedule we already discussed. What do the rides do to the difference?

From The Higgins, allow about $174 total: airport transfers, one round trip to City Park, and a modest evening ride allowance. That puts airfare, lodging, and local transportation at $2,823.40: $1,074 + $1,575.40 + $174. From the City Park property, allow about $296 because the museums, music evening, and central-area meals require more trips. Its complete estimate is $2,749.76: $1,074 + $1,379.76 + $296.
So City Park is only $73.64 less after transportation, correct?
Correct. The lodging gap is $195.64, but about $122 of additional rides reduces the overall difference to $73.64. Both plans remain below the $3,200 trip ceiling.

I do prefer breakfast being included when a hotel offers it, especially for three of us. But I don't think that offsets putting our daughter on a sleeper sofa and adding rides for most of the itinerary.

That tradeoff favors The Higgins. The City Park property has the lower total and includes breakfast, but The Higgins gives you two queen beds and walkable access to the two museum visits and the evening music plans. The City Park outing is the only substantial excursion from the Warehouse District.

Keep The Higgins, then. Before anything is booked, make sure the destination fee really is included in that $1,575.40 and that the one-night deposit is refundable under the stated deadline. I don't want a second fee appearing at checkout.

The Higgins remains selected, with no reservation made. The room is displayed for two adults and one 14-year-old in two queen beds. The working lodging total is $1,575.40, including $1,327.40 in room and taxes plus the four $62 destination fees; one night is due at booking and the remainder at the hotel. Before purchase, obtain a final checkout page confirming no additional mandatory fee and that the deposit returns to the original payment method when canceled by 6:00 p.m. Central on October 7. With estimated rides, the trip remains $2,823.40, or $376.60 under budget.
